extracted.intended_audience: Persons or organizations petitioning the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to issue, amend, or rescind regulations under 10 CFR chapter I
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural guidance for filing a petition for rulemaking with the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission under 10 CFR 2.802, including content requirements, permitted staff consultations, and amendment/withdrawal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file and addressed recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may petition the Commission to issue, amend, or rescind any regulation in 10 CFR chapter I. The petition should be addressed to the Secretary, Attention: Rulemakings and Adjudications Staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods of submission: by mail to U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Washington, DC 20555-0001; by email to Rulemaking.Comments@nrc.gov; or by hand delivery to 11555 Rockville Pike, Rockville, Maryland 20852 between 7:30 a.m. and 4:15 p.m. (Eastern time) on Federal workdays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted consultation with NRC staff
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may consult with the NRC staff before and after filing by contacting the Chief, Regulatory Analysis and Rulemaking Support Branch, Division of Rulemaking, Environmental, and Financial Support, Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff may assist with describing the process for filing, docketing, tracking, closing, amending, withdrawing, and resolving a petition for rulemaking; clarifying an existing NRC regulation and the basis for the regulation; and assisting the petitioner to clarify a petition so the Commission can understand the petitioner's issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on staff assistance (no drafting of text)
rubrics_metrics.description: In consultation, NRC staff will not draft or develop text or alternative approaches to address matters in the petition for rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff assistance is limited to procedural description and clarification; they must not produce regulatory language or alternative solutions for the petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on staff advice (no counsel on amendment/withdrawal)
rubrics_metrics.description: NRC staff will not advise a petitioner on whether a petition should be amended or withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should not expect staff to provide recommendations about petition status decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contact and identification information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition must clearly and concisely specify the name of the petitioner, a telephone number, a mailing address, and an email address (if available) that the NRC may use to communicate with the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete contact information to ensure the NRC can communicate regarding docketing and disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational petitioner identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner is an organization, provide additional identifying information as applicable including the petitioner's organizational or corporate status, State of incorporation, registered agent, and the name and authority of the individual who signed the petition on behalf of the organizational or corporate petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include corporate details and signatory authority to establish organizational standing and point of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of problems or issues to be addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the specific problems or issues that the petitioner believes should be addressed through rulemaking, including any specific circumstances in which the NRC's codified requirements are incorrect, incomplete, inadequate, or unnecessarily burdensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe concrete examples or circumstances demonstrating why current requirements are deficient or burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting publicly-available data or information
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite, enclose, or reference publicly-available technical, scientific, or other data or information supporting the petitioner's assertion of the problems or issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations or copies of the evidence relied upon; publicly-available sources are required for substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed solution (including specific regulatory language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the petitioner's proposed solution to the problems or issues raised in the petition for rulemaking (e.g., a proposed solution may include specific regulations or regulatory language to add to, amend in, or delete from 10 CFR chapter I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete regulatory edits or proposed language when possible to show the exact change sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis showing how the proposal solves the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an analysis, discussion, or argument that explains how the petitioner's proposed solution solves the problems or issues identified by the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the proposed regulatory text to the problem statement and supporting evidence; show causal or logical links between the proposal and resolution of identified issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional supporting information for the proposed solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite, enclose, or reference any other publicly-available data or information supporting the petitioner's proposed solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include materials that specifically support why the proposed change is warranted and feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental report when required (Petitioner's Environmental Report)
rubrics_metrics.description: If required by 10 CFR 51.68, submit a separate document entitled 'Petitioner's Environmental Report,' which contains the information specified in 10 CFR 51.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an environmental report is required, follow the content requirements in 10 CFR 51.45 and submit it as a separate attachment to the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain NRC authority to adopt the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist the NRC in its evaluation, the petitioner should clearly and concisely explain why the proposed rulemaking solution is within the authority of the NRC to adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide legal or statutory basis demonstrating that the NRC has jurisdiction and authority to make the requested regulatory change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain why rulemaking is the appropriate remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist evaluation, the petitioner should explain why rulemaking is the most favorable approach to address the problem or issue, as opposed to other NRC actions such as licensing, issuance of an order, or referral to another Federal or State agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare alternatives and justify why rulemaking (versus other remedies) is necessary or preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of lead petitioner for multiple petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition is signed by multiple petitioners, the petition must designate a lead petitioner who is responsible for disseminating communications received from the NRC to co-petitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a single contact responsible for communications and distribution to co-petitioners to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for suspension of adjudication involving licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner may request the Commission to suspend all or any part of any licensing proceeding to which the petitioner is a participant pending disposition of the petition for rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear request and specify which proceedings or parts are to be suspended if seeking suspension pending the petition's resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment or withdrawal of a docketed petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner wants to amend or withdraw a docketed petition for rulemaking, the petitioner should include the docket number and the date that the original petition was submitted in a filing addressed to the Secretary, Attention: Rulemakings and Adjudications Staff, and sent by mail or email to Rulemaking.Comments@nrc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference docket number and original submission date so the NRC can correctly identify the petition to be amended or withdrawn; use same mailing/email channels as original filing.
